content: Section 5 of the Standards of Care in Diabetes—2024 focuses on strategies to promote positive health behaviors and enhance overall well-being, with the ultimate goal of improving health outcomes for individuals with diabetes. It emphasizes the importance of patient-centered care, which involves tailoring interventions to the unique needs, preferences, and circumstances of each individual. The section highlights the role of diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) as a cornerstone of effective diabetes care. DSMES programs are designed to provide individuals with the knowledge, skills, and confidence necessary to manage their condition effectively. These programs should address key areas such as healthy eating, physical activity, medication adherence, blood glucose monitoring, and problem-solving for diabetes-related challenges. Behavioral and psychological support is also emphasized as a critical component of care. This includes identifying and addressing mental health conditions such as depression, anxiety, and diabetes distress, which can significantly impact self-care behaviors and overall health outcomes. Providers are encouraged to screen for these conditions regularly and offer appropriate interventions, including counseling or referral to mental health professionals when needed. The section underscores the importance of promoting healthy lifestyle behaviors, including regular physical activity and a balanced diet. It provides evidence-based recommendations for physical activity, such as engaging in at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise per week, along with resistance training and flexibility exercises. Nutritional guidance should be individualized, taking into account cultural preferences, personal goals, and metabolic needs. Additionally, the section addresses the role of technology in supporting positive health behaviors. Tools such as continuous glucose monitors (CGMs), mobile health applications, and telehealth services can enhance patient engagement and provide real-time feedback to support self-management efforts. Finally, the section calls for a collaborative approach to care, involving a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals, including physicians, nurses, dietitians, and mental health specialists.
